hiddenTests.description: The grader. replay_attempt.description: Read the attempt's own log: every recorded event in order — edits, runs, submissions, verdicts — with its offset from when the attempt opened, plus one line per test case inside every run with its expected/actual values. Nothing in it is summarised or interpreted; it is what was recorded. Two derived sections come with it because a log in order cannot show them: each case's verdict across every run (a transpose) and each run's newly-passing and newly-failing cases (a diff). Take the whole log when the attempt is small — that is the default — and use the parameters to narrow it when it is long or when you only need one metric. This is the sharpest instrument you have for aiming the next question: a 6/7 reached by fixing one case in ninety seconds and a 6/7 reached by breaking two others are different learners.

caseDetail.description: `brief` drops the expected/actual pair from each failing case line in the log. Default full.

cases.description: Narrow the case history. `still-failing` is what is wrong now; `fixed` is what they repaired themselves, which is evidence of learning inside one attempt.

eventTypes.description: Keep only these event types in the log, e.g. ["test_run"] for nothing but the runs, or ["file_changed","test_run"] for the edit-and-run rhythm. Omit for every type. Recorded types: attempt_started, file_changed, command_executed, test_run, submission_created, submission_evaluated, attempt_completed, hint_requested, learner_remark, agent_message.

maxLines.description: Cap on log lines, newest kept, and it says how many it dropped. Default 400. Raise it rather than guessing at what a truncated log left out.

scope.description: `since-last-submission` keeps only what happened after the last graded run, which is often the whole question on a follow-up turn.

sections.description: log: every event, in order, with its payload and per-case lines. cases: each case's verdict in every run, with pass and failure counts. runs: each run's score and which cases newly passed or newly failed against the last run that saw them. timings: totals, the gap before the first run, the longest gap between events, and each edit stretch. Defaults to log, cases and runs.

review_solution.description: Judge HOW the passing solution was written, after the runner has already settled that it works. Send it back only for a requirement the challenge actually stated, or for a solution that defeats the point of the exercise — hardcoding the test inputs, calling a library that does the whole thing being taught, or a complexity class the challenge ruled out. A different-but-legitimate approach is not grounds for rework.

observedComplexity.description: The time complexity of what they actually wrote, e.g. "O(n)" or "O(n log n) from the sort".

reasons.description: For `rework`, the requirement missed and what to change — no solution, still only the nudge. For `accepted`, what made it a good use of the idea. Written to the learner.

verdict.description: `rework` reopens the challenge for the learner and ends your turn here — no ability update and no next challenge. Use it only when you can name the stated requirement it misses.

Returns a compact digest of the run: which lines ran and how often, which way every branch went, what each variable started and ended as. Never trace a working solution to the challenge the learner is currently on.
